questions.question: Why does the CDK `Overlay` render content into a container attached to `document.body`?
options: To make the content load lazily
So floating UI escapes parent `overflow: hidden` and z-index stacking contexts
Because overlays cannot use Angular templates
To avoid running change detection on it
questions.explanation: Dropdowns, tooltips and dialogs get clipped or hidden by ancestor styles; rendering them in a body-level overlay container avoids that.

questions.question: After a filter runs, you want screen readers to announce '42 transactions found' without moving focus. Which CDK service fits?
questions.explanation: LiveAnnouncer writes the message into a visually hidden aria-live region, which screen readers announce.

questions.question: Which statement about CDK virtual scrolling is correct?
options: It uses the `*cdkVirtualFor` directive inside a `cdk-virtual-scroll-viewport` that has a fixed height
It works with the built-in `@for` block automatically
It renders all rows but hides off-screen ones with CSS
It requires Angular Material to be installed
questions.explanation: Only rows near the viewport are rendered. The viewport needs a fixed CSS height and an `itemSize`, and iteration uses `*cdkVirtualFor`, not `@for`.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a requirement for an accessible modal dialog?
options: Focus is trapped inside the dialog while it is open
Focus returns to the triggering element when the dialog closes
The dialog must be rendered with `@defer`
The container has `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"` and an accessible name via `aria-labelledby`
questions.explanation: Deferring has nothing to do with accessibility. The real requirements are role/aria attributes, focus trapping, Escape to close, focus restoration and hiding background content.
